exposure: socioeconomic disadvantage (lower household income, lone parental status, lower socioeconomic indexes for area)
maternal health factors (younger maternal age, maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, higher gestational weight gain, prenatal maternal stress, maternal prenatal depression)
maternal lifestyle factors (prenatal alcohol, maternal smoking frequency)
environmental air pollutant exposures (particulate matter < 2.5 um at birth, child secondhand tobacco smoke at 12 months)
home environment (dampness/mould, home heating with oil, kerosene or diesel heaters at 2 years postnatal)
outcome: autism spectrum disorder symptoms at age 2 years
autism spectrum disorder diagnosis by age 4 years
cohort: The study participants were children from the population-derived Barwon Infant Study cohort, with outcomes assessed at 2 and 4 years of age.
finding: Lower socioeconomic indexes for area, later birth order, higher maternal prenatal depression, and maternal smoking frequency showed a dose-response relationship with autism spectrum disorder symptoms at age 2 years.
